problem_definition: Thrombus formation on mechanical heart valves causing obstruction
baseline_architecture: Mechanical heart valves currently allow platelet adhesion and coagulation activation on their blood-contacting surfaces
inventive_nucleus: A thin, porous, and negatively charged nanofiber mesh is integrated around the mechanical heart valve to mimic the natural glycocalyx and reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation, while also incorporating a shear-resistant material and a dynamic control system to adapt to changing blood flow conditions.
mechanism: The nanofiber mesh interacts with the blood flowing through the mechanical heart valve, reducing platelet adhesion and coagulation activation.
causal_chain: Thrombus formation on the mechanical heart valve
Nanofiber mesh reduces platelet adhesion and coagulation activation
Nanofiber mesh's surface charge and porosity are adjusted in real-time
Dynamic control system adapts to changing blood flow conditions
Reduced platelet adhesion and coagulation activation
Reduced risk of mechanical heart valve failure
system_architecture: The nanofiber mesh is co-located with the mechanical heart valve and is secured using a biocompatible adhesive. The negatively charged nanoparticles are evenly distributed across the nanofiber mesh.
control_logic: step1: nanofiber mesh is integrated around the mechanical heart valve
step2: nanofiber mesh is secured using a biocompatible adhesive
operating_conditions: The nanofiber mesh operates under normal blood flow conditions.
boundary_conditions: The nanofiber mesh is designed to fail safely by releasing from the mechanical heart valve in the event of excessive mechanical interference.
expected_effect: Reduced thrombus formation on the mechanical heart valve.
technical_advantage: The nanofiber mesh's ability to reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation is directly correlated with its surface charge and porosity.
The nanofiber mesh is coated with a layer of negatively charged nanoparticles to enhance its ability to reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation.
The dynamic control system adjusts the nanofiber mesh's surface charge and porosity in real-time to adapt to changing blood flow conditions.
novelty_hypothesis: The combination of a shear-resistant material and a dynamic control system to adapt to changing blood flow conditions, in conjunction with the integration of a thin, porous, and negatively charged nanofiber mesh around the mechanical heart valve.
